group.passage: Every time someone streams a video or asks a chatbot a question, the request travels to a data center, a building packed with computers that run day and night. Those machines turn electricity into heat, and unless the heat is carried away, they cannot keep working properly. Carrying it away often takes water, and a surprising amount of it. Many large data centers rely on cooling towers. Warm water from the cooling system is pumped into the towers, where part of it evaporates and takes the heat into the air. Water that leaves as vapor does not return to the river or lake it came from, so experts describe it as consumed rather than simply used. The remaining water can circulate several times, but each round of evaporation leaves minerals behind, and once they become too concentrated, the water must be drained away and replaced. Because more water evaporates in hot weather, these centers are thirstiest in the hottest hours of the day and the hottest months of the year. One study estimated that American data centers directly used about 17 billion gallons of water in 2023, roughly three times the 5.6 billion gallons used in 2014. That figure leaves out a hidden share. Many of the power plants that supply data centers with electricity cool themselves with towers of their own, so every unit of power carries a water cost. The International Energy Agency estimates that only about 40 percent of the water linked to data centers is used on site; the other 60 percent is consumed at power plants. Reducing this footprint is harder than it sounds. Air-cooled systems use no water at all, but they need more electricity than systems that depend on evaporation. Timing offers another option. Training runs for AI models, which can take weeks, are a different matter from everyday requests. Unlike web searches and video streams, which users expect to start instantly, they can be scheduled for almost any hour, including cooler ones when less water is lost. Yet the coolest hours are rarely the sunniest, so the time that saves the most water may not be the time when solar power is most plentiful.

第三段說的「隱藏的份額」是什麼？

2.explanation_zh: 第四段說氣冷系統完全不用水，但比靠蒸發的系統更耗電。所以把冷卻塔換成氣冷，資料中心本身的用水會減少，用電卻會增加。第三段又說發電廠也耗水，所以總用水量不一定會消失。

option_notes_zh.B: 細節錯置：天熱時蒸發較多，所以是炎熱的時段最需要水；而且換成氣冷後根本不靠蒸發。

3.strategy_zh: 數字題要自己算：「增加多少」用減法（17 − 5.6），「幾倍」用除法；也要分清楚 40% 和 60% 各指哪裡的用水。

translation_zh.text:
每當有人串流影片或問聊天機器人一個問題，這個請求就會傳送到資料中心——一棟擠滿日夜運轉的電腦的建築。這些機器把電轉換成熱，如果不把熱帶走，它們就無法正常運作。而帶走熱量往往需要用水，而且用量驚人。
許多大型資料中心依靠冷卻塔。冷卻系統的溫水被抽進冷卻塔，部分的水在那裡蒸發，把熱帶進空氣中。以水蒸氣形式離開的水不會回到原本取水的河流或湖泊，所以專家說這些水是被「消耗」掉，而不只是「使用」。剩下的水可以循環好幾次，但每一輪蒸發都會留下礦物質；一旦礦物質太濃，這些水就必須排掉並換新。因為天氣熱時蒸發的水比較多，這些資料中心在一天中最熱的時段、一年中最熱的月份最「口渴」。一項研究估計，美國的資料中心在 2023 年直接用掉約 170 億加侖的水，大約是 2014 年 56 億加侖的三倍。
這個數字還漏掉了一部分隱藏的用水。許多為資料中心供電的發電廠，也用自己的冷卻塔降溫，所以每一度電都伴隨著用水的代價。國際能源署估計，與資料中心有關的用水中，只有約 40% 是在現場使用，其餘 60% 消耗在發電廠。
要減少這個用水足跡，比聽起來困難。氣冷系統完全不用水，但比靠蒸發的系統需要更多電力。調整時間是另一個選項。AI 模型的訓練工作可能要花上好幾週，和日常的請求不一樣。不同於使用者期待立刻開始的網路搜尋與影片串流，訓練工作幾乎可以安排在任何時段，包括水分流失較少的涼爽時段。然而，最涼爽的時段很少是陽光最充足的時段，所以最省水的時間，未必是太陽能最充沛的時間。

open_tasks.prompt: A company wants to build a new data center in a hot, dry area. Based on the passage, give one piece of advice in 1–2 English sentences and explain the trade-off involved.
reference_answers: The company could use air-cooled systems to protect the local water supply, but it should also buy clean electricity, because air cooling uses more power and power plants also consume water.
The company could schedule AI training for cooler night hours to lose less water, even though this means it cannot rely on solar power at those times.
